title: Advanced Phrasal Verbs: Multiple Meanings
completion_message: ¡Bienvenido al Nivel C2: Maestría! En este nivel exploraremos los matices más finos del inglés. Muchos Phrasal Verbs cambian radicalmente de significado según el contexto, y dominarlos es la marca definitiva del bilingüismo perfecto.

parts.visual:
1. TAKE IN 
- Entender/Asimilar: It was too much information to take in. 
- Engañar: We were completely taken in by his charm. 
- Alojar/Acoger: She took in stray dogs. 

2. PUT DOWN 
- Criticar/Humillar: Stop putting yourself down. 
- Anotar: Put down your name on the list. 
- Sacrificar (un animal): We had to put our old dog down.
parts.audio: Welcome to Level C2. Number 1: Take in. It can mean to understand or absorb information: It was too much information to take in. It can mean to deceive: We were completely taken in by his charm. It can also mean to provide shelter: She took in stray dogs. Number 2: Put down. It can mean to criticize or humiliate: Stop putting yourself down. To write something: Put down your name on the list. Or to euthanize an animal: We had to put our old dog down.

parts.visual:
3. MAKE OUT 
- Distinguir/Ver con dificultad: I couldn't make out the sign in the fog. 
- Entender a alguien/algo: I can't make him out. 
- Besar apasionadamente (informal): They were making out in the car. 

4. PULL OFF 
- Lograr algo difícil: We managed to pull off the deal at the last minute. 
- Arrancar (vehículo) hacia un lado: Pull off the road when it's safe.
parts.audio: Number 3: Make out. It can mean to see or hear with difficulty: I couldn't make out the sign in the fog. To understand someone's character: I can't make him out. Or, informally, to kiss passionately. Number 4: Pull off. It means to succeed in doing something very difficult: We managed to pull off the deal at the last minute. Or, for a vehicle, to leave the road: Pull off the road when it's safe.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el significado correcto del phrasal verb en su contexto.

questions.question: The lecture was very complex. It was a lot of information to take ____. (Asimilar).
Don't buy that fake watch! Don't be taken ____ by their lies. (Engañado).
The boss is always putting me ____ in front of the team. (Humillando/Criticando).
questions.explanation: Put down = humillar o criticar negativamente.

questions.question: Please put ____ your contact details on this form. (Anotar).
The horse was badly injured and had to be put ____. (Sacrificado).
questions.explanation: Put down = aplicar eutanasia a un animal.

questions.question: It was so dark I couldn't make ____ the numbers on the house. (Distinguir visualmente).
questions.explanation: Make out = distinguir algo con dificultad visual o auditiva.

questions.question: He is a very strange guy; I really can't make him ____. (Entender su personalidad).
questions.explanation: Make someone out = entender cómo es alguien.

questions.question: Winning the championship with an injured team was hard, but they pulled it ____. (Lograr algo difícil).
questions.explanation: Pull off = lograr algo con éxito contra todo pronóstico.

questions.question: I heard a strange noise in the engine, so I pulled ____ to the side of the road. (Apartarse en el coche).
questions.explanation: Pull off / pull over = apartarse de la carretera.

questions.question: She makes ____ that she is rich, but she actually has a lot of debt. (Fingir/Aparentar).
questions.explanation: Make out = fingir o afirmar algo que no es cierto.

questions.question: The tailor had to take the suit ____ because I lost weight. (Estrechar ropa).
questions.explanation: Take in (clothes) = hacer más pequeña/estrecha una prenda.

questions.question: The rebel army tried to take ____ the government. (Tomar el control).
We were completely taken ____ by the scam email. (Engañados).
I need a minute to take ____ the beauty of this landscape. (Absorber/Disfrutar).
questions.explanation: Take in = absorber visual o mentalmente.

questions.question: To avoid a crash, the driver pulled ____ at the last second. (Desviarse bruscamente).
If you don't wear glasses, you won't be able to make ____ the letters. (Distinguir).
They told us the project was cancelled, which really put us ____. (Desanimar/Causar molestia).
questions.explanation: Put out = causar molestia o inconveniencia (I was very put out).

questions.question: The firemen managed to put ____ the fire quickly. (Extinguir).
We had to put ____ the meeting until next week. (Posponer).
It was a very ambitious plan, but the CEO managed to pull it ____. (Lograrlo).
Take ____ the information. (Asimilar)
He was taken ____ by a scam. (Engañado)
Don't put yourself ____. (Humillarse)
Put ____ your name. (Anotar)
Make ____ the sign in the dark. (Distinguir)
I can't make him ____. (Entenderlo)
We pulled it ____! (Lo logramos)
Pull ____ the road. (Apartarse del camino)
Put ____ the fire. (Extinguir)
Take the suit ____. (Hacer más pequeño)
